title: Smooth locality and flat descent of local finite type for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], their fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] and their field-valued point classes [def-weil-field]. Locally of finite type for an algebraic-space map is tested on compatible etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The property $\mathcal P=$ locally of finite type is smooth local on source-and-target: (i) precomposing a locally finite type map with a smooth map preserves local finite type; (ii) smooth base change preserves local finite type; (iii) a map $r:X\to Y$ is locally of finite type if and only if, for each $x\in|X|$, there are algebraic spaces $U,V$, smooth maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, a point $u\in|U|$ with $a(u)=x$, and a locally finite type map $h:U\to V$ with $r a=b h$. Moreover local finite type is fpqc local, and hence fppf local, on the target: if $\{Y_i\to Y\}$ is such a covering, then $r$ is locally of finite type if and only if every $X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i$ is locally of finite type. Coverings of algebraic spaces mean families whose scheme pullbacks are coverings in the corresponding topology; the scheme notions are [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering, def-pc-fppf-site].

proof.text: First verify fppf source locality for schemes. Let $q_i:T_i\to T$ be an fppf covering and $f:T\to Z$ a scheme map. If $f$ is locally of finite type, so is every $fq_i$: local finite presentation implies local finite type, and the latter is closed under composition. Conversely, suppose all $fq_i$ are locally of finite type. Form the scheme $Q=\coprod_iT_i$. Its component inclusions are open immersions and cover $Q$. Open-source locality of flatness and local finite presentation shows that $q:Q\to T$ has both properties. The covering condition makes $q$ surjective. Open-source locality of local finite type applied to the component maps shows $fq$ locally of finite type. Apply the scheme flat-lfp source-descent theorem to $q$ and $f$ to obtain local finite type of $f$. This includes $T=\varnothing$ and the empty covering: $Q=\varnothing$, and all the local conditions are vacuous.

The scheme property locally of finite type is etale local on source-and-target by the scheme locality node. Its algebraic-space extension is exactly the etale presentation property, and agrees with the convention in this item. Step 1 verifies the scheme fppf source-locality hypothesis of the transfer lemma. Apply that lemma with $P=$ locally of finite type. Thus for every fppf covering $\{A_j\to A\}$ of algebraic spaces and every $g:A\to B$, $g$ is locally of finite type if and only if every $A_j\to B$ is locally of finite type.

All maps of algebraic spaces are representable by algebraic spaces: each scheme pullback is an algebraic space by the fibre-product theorem. Hence the representable chartwise calculus applies to them. Smooth maps are locally of finite presentation and therefore locally of finite type. Composition now gives (i), and arbitrary base-change stability of local finite type gives (ii), in particular for a smooth base change. For (iii), the forward implication uses $U=X,V=Y,a=\mathrm{id}_X,b=\mathrm{id}_Y,h=r$ and $u=x$. Conversely choose the data in (iii) for every $x$. Each $b_xh_x=ra_x$ is locally of finite type by smoothness of $b_x$ and composition. The smooth family $\{a_x:U_x\to X\}_{x\in|X|}$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and jointly surjective since $u_x$ maps to $x$; it is an fppf covering. Step 2 gives local finite type of $r$. The empty source uses its empty covering, so no nonemptiness is assumed.

proof.text: For fpqc descent, verify the three hypotheses of the affine-test criterion with $P=$ locally of finite type. First it is closed under finite disjoint unions. The space coproduct theorem gives the finite source and target coproducts, choosing scheme atlases within the fixed universe. The sheaf-coproduct partition theorem says that every scheme test of a component inclusion is an open-and-closed subscheme; hence that inclusion is an open subspace and is etale by the open-chart test. On each source component the union map is its given locally finite type map followed by this etale target inclusion. The chartwise calculus gives local finite type of that composite and, by open-source locality, of the union map. The nullary case is $\varnothing\to\varnothing$: its compatible scheme charts have empty source, and the affine-cover definition of local finite type is vacuous. Thus finite-union closure includes the empty union.

source.place: Tag 041S (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type), hypothesis (1) of Tag 041J; empty-union case explicit.

proof.text: For affine detection, arbitrary base-change stability gives the forward implication. Conversely suppose every affine scheme base change of $f:X\to Y$ is locally of finite type. Choose an etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a scheme atlas $U\to X\times_YV$. Cover $V$ by affine opens $V_j$. Each $U_j=U\times_VV_j$ is an open subscheme of $U$, and is an etale surjective atlas of $X\times_YV_j$ by etale base change. The chart test and the assumed property over $V_j$ give local finite type of $U_j\to V_j$. Compose with the open immersion $V_j\to V$; composition and open-source locality give local finite type of $U\to V$. The chart test then gives local finite type of $f$. This uses no affine-intersection or quasi-compactness assumption.

source.place: Tag 041S, hypothesis (2) of Tag 041J, using spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 040Y (lemma-finite-type-local).

proof.text: For the remaining hypothesis let $Z'\to Z$ be flat surjective between affine schemes, and suppose $X\times_ZZ'\to Z'$ locally of finite type. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X$. Its pullback $U'=U\times_ZZ'\to X\times_ZZ'$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas. The chart test over $Z'$ gives local finite type of the scheme map $U'\to Z'$. The singleton $\{Z'\to Z\}$ is an fpqc covering: the map $g:Z'\to Z$ is flat, and an affine open $V\subset Z$ is quasi-compact, so $V=\bigcup_{k=1}^nD(t_k)$ for finitely many standard opens of the affine scheme $Z$; the standard opens $D(g^*t_k)=g^{-1}(D(t_k))$ of $Z'$ are affine and, $g$ being surjective, their images cover $V$. Scheme fpqc descent therefore gives local finite type of $U\to Z$. The chart test over $Z$ gives local finite type of $X\to Z$. With Steps 4 and 5, all hypotheses of the affine-test criterion hold. Applying it proves the asserted equivalence for every fpqc covering in the sense of the criterion; Step 7 shows that the coverings of the item are of this kind.

source.place: Tag 041S (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type), affine faithfully flat reduction and application of Tag 041J.

proof.text: Finally the coverings of the item are fpqc coverings in the sense of the criterion. For an fpqc covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$ of the item and a scheme $T\to Y$, choose surjective etale scheme atlases $E_i\to Y_i\times_YT$; the scheme pullback family $\{E_i\to T\}$ is a scheme fpqc covering. Its maps are flat, which is flatness of $Y_i\to Y$ on etale scheme charts, and for $T$ affine the definition of scheme fpqc coverings applied to the affine open $T$ gives finitely many affine opens of the $E_i$, flat over $T$, whose images cover $T$ and which map to the $Y_i$ over $Y$. Next an fppf covering is fpqc in the same sense. For an affine scheme $T\to Y$, choose etale surjective scheme atlases $E_i\to Y_i\times_YT$. By base change and composition, the maps $E_i\to T$ are flat and locally of finite presentation; they jointly cover $T$. Thus they form a scheme fppf covering. The finite affine refinement lemma supplies finitely many affine opens in the $E_i$ mapping jointly surjectively to $T$. These maps are flat and factor through the $Y_i$, which is precisely the required standard fpqc refinement. Flatness of $Y_i\to Y$ is already part of the fppf hypothesis. Consequently Step 6 applies to fppf coverings too. Empty affine tests allow the empty refinement.
